items_to_review: Educator review of wording, item mix and the three-word limitation.
en-US TTS reading of the bare letter 'A.', 'A says a' and the words (EN-6).

English: check item 1 asks for the SMALL letter a (listening) and practice item 1 asks the partner of small a, so both cases are tested; the letter name A versus the sound 'a' as spoken by en-US TTS is unverified.
notes: TASK ORDER: the 'which word does NOT begin with the letter' puzzle is taught in demonstrate step 5, practised in guided 3 and practice 5, and used again only in remediation guided 1. It is NOT used in the check: with three words two words never begin with the letter, so a three-option version has two right answers and a two-option version is a 50% guess.

GUESS RATE: every check and remediation-check item has 3 options (a blind guess is 33%; passing 2 of 3 by guessing alone is about 26%). The thresholds are data fields; with only three words the guess rate cannot be lowered further in this pilot.

PILOT LIMITATION: only three picture words exist for this letter, so check and remediation items reuse the same three words. Items differ by task type (listen-to-word to letter, which word does NOT begin with the letter, picture naming without a caption, listen-to-letter to picture), option sets and distractor letters, but a child can still learn the three words by memory. More human-approved picture words are required before rollout.
Question pictures carry an empty caption so the answer is never printed on screen; teaching steps keep captions.
Audio-only items (visual none) need a replay button and a visual fallback if text-to-speech fails (UI decision).
No tracing / stroke order is taught.

After a failed check the child gets remediation (different explanation, 2 guided, 3 alternate check items), at most max_remediation_cycles times; then the UI marks the concept 'needs support' (after_limit offer_parent_support) and lets the child continue.

No tracing / stroke order is taught.

After a failed check the child gets remediation (different explanation, 2 guided, 3 alternate check items), at most max_remediation_cycles times; then the UI marks the concept 'needs support' (after_limit offer_parent_support) and lets the child continue.

items_to_review: Every sentence (text, speech, prompts, hints, feedback, explanations) is AI-written and UNVERIFIED by a native speaker: grammar, naturalness, register and age suitability.
Text-to-speech in the lesson locale was not heard: how a lone letter is read (letter name versus sound, vowel length), and every sentence.
The word used for 'picture' in prompts is not an existing picture-word vocabulary item; confirm it is acceptable.
Negative prompt ('which word does NOT begin with the letter') is a difficulty-3 item: educator and native speaker to confirm the wording is clear for a young child and the task is suitable.
Sound-first remediation sentences ('close your eyes and listen', 'the first sound is the sound of the letter') need native checking of phrasing and of what 'sound of the letter' should be called.
The letter distractors in letter-choice items are the first letters of the other two picture words; confirm they are acceptable distractors.
Whether each picture file clearly shows its word (te_amma and ta_mother show two people; a child may name them differently).

Tamil: sandhi fixed in 'எழுத்தைக் கவனமாகப்' and in 'நீங்கள் ... என்ற சொல்லைக் கேட்டீர்கள்' (the verifier's findings) - fixes are still unverified; also 'ஒலி' for sound, 'தொடங்காத', 'நினைவில் வைத்துக்கொள்ளுங்கள்', register.
notes: TASK ORDER: the 'which word does NOT begin with the letter' puzzle is taught in demonstrate step 5, practised in guided 3 and practice 5, and used again only in remediation guided 1. It is NOT used in the check: with three words two words never begin with the letter, so a three-option version has two right answers and a two-option version is a 50% guess.

GUESS RATE: every check and remediation-check item has 3 options (a blind guess is 33%; passing 2 of 3 by guessing alone is about 26%). The thresholds are data fields; with only three words the guess rate cannot be lowered further in this pilot.

PILOT LIMITATION: only three picture words exist for this letter, so check and remediation items reuse the same three words. Items differ by task type (listen-to-word to letter, which word does NOT begin with the letter, picture naming without a caption, listen-to-letter to picture), option sets and distractor letters, but a child can still learn the three words by memory. More human-approved picture words are required before rollout.
Question pictures carry an empty caption so the answer is never printed on screen; teaching steps keep captions.
Audio-only items (visual none) need a replay button and a visual fallback if text-to-speech fails (UI decision).
No tracing / stroke order is taught.

After a failed check the child gets remediation (different explanation, 2 guided, 3 alternate check items), at most max_remediation_cycles times; then the UI marks the concept 'needs support' (after_limit offer_parent_support) and lets the child continue.

items_to_review: PREREQUISITE REVIEW: num-count (curriculum.dart) only counts three stars, but num-add needs counting to 10, reading a 0-10 number line, the + and = signs and counting on. This lesson teaches those inside (introduce 1-2, demonstrate 2, 4, 5) rather than assuming them; an educator should decide whether the prerequisite should change or this inline teaching is enough.

Educator review of the concrete -> pictorial -> symbolic progression, the count-on strategy, pass marks, and whether symbolic items 5+4, 7+2, 7+1 are sufficiently scaffolded by the equation step and hint ladder.
en-IN TTS reading of number words, 'plus', 'equals', 'count on'.
Emoji rendering (💎 ⭐ 🌟 🚀 🍎 🍓 🌙) on the target device; the intro crystal artwork (num_crystal.webp) is no longer used, objects are emoji.
New visual fields showHops / showResult are not implemented anywhere yet (see content/teaching/SCHEMA.md).
Make-ten facts (8+2, 6+4) were REMOVED because they were never taught; all sums here are solved by counting on.
notes: All answers independently computed; every distractor is wrong; distractor patterns vary (a starting number, a near miss, a distant number) and the key is not always in the same position. Options are stored in a mixed order; the UI may shuffle.
Check and remediation-check number-line items set showHops false and objects items showResult false, so the answer is not drawn; guided number-line items show the hops (scaffold).
After a failed check: remediation (count-on explanation, 2 guided, 3 alternate check items), at most max_remediation_cycles times, then 'needs support' (offer_parent_support); the child can continue.
Each operand pair is used once (either order) across the whole lesson.
